Advantages.heading: Unique Features
Advantages.intro: DEX223 introduces a number of revolutionary concepts that no other exchange implements in the same way currently. These features will drastically improve the security, make token listings as easy and transparent as possible and allow on-platform lending of assets.

marginTrading.heading: Encapsulated margin trading
marginTrading.intro: DEX223 introduces an innovative lending mechanism that enables users to create “lending orders” with full control over terms and conditions. Here’s how it works:

lendingOrders.heading: Flexible lending orders
lendingOrders.funds: Funds: Place any token in your lending order.
lendingOrders.interestRate: Interest Rate & Deadline: Define your desired annualized interest rate and loan duration.
lendingOrders.permittedMarkets: Permitted Markets: Specify which markets the borrower can trade on.
lendingOrders.collateral: Collateral & Configuration: Require a minimum collateral amount and set optional parameters for customization.

funds.title: Any token
funds.text: Place any token in your lending order.

terms.title: Rate and deadline
terms.text: Set the annual interest rate and loan duration.

markets.title: Permitted markets
markets.text: Choose which markets the borrower can trade on.

collateral.title: Collateral and settings
collateral.text: Require minimum collateral and set optional parameters.

borrowerAccess.heading: Borrower access & control
borrowerAccess.deposit: A borrower deposits the required collateral to accept your lending order.
borrowerAccess.trade: They gain the ability to trade with the borrowed funds on the permitted markets but cannot withdraw those funds from DEX223.
borrowerAccess.security: This ensures the lender maintains ultimate security while still allowing the borrower to engage in active market strategies.

deposit.title: Collateral first
deposit.text: Borrowers deposit collateral to accept your order.

trade.title: Trade, never withdraw
trade.text: Funds trade on permitted markets but stay on DEX223.

liquidation.expectedBalance: The lender sets an “expected balance” for the borrower’s positions at any moment during the loan. For example, if 15 ETH is lent at 20% for 30 days, the borrower’s cumulative balance must be 18 ETH on day 30 or 16.5 ETH on day 15.
liquidation.actualBalance: At any point, the borrower’s actual balance is measured by the immediate market sell value of all their positions (accounting for liquidity).
liquidation.trigger: If the actual balance falls below the expected balance, anyone can trigger liquidation in return for a small reward, defined by the lender at order creation.
liquidation.autoClose: Liquidation automatically closes the borrower’s positions on the spot, protecting the lender’s investment.
liquidation.noOracles: This self-contained approach removes reliance on external price oracles, bolstering security and transparency.
liquidation.title: Liquidation protection

expected.text: You set the balance the borrower must hold over time.

trigger.text: Below that balance, anyone can close the positions for a reward.

noOracles.title: No price oracles
noOracles.text: Balances use real market sell value, not external oracles.

erc223Support.heading: ERC-223 Support
erc223Support.losses: Integrating ERC-223 directly addresses a key shortcoming of the ERC-20 design, which has led to the loss of approximately $201,690,000 worth of tokens on Ethereum mainnet as of 29 August 2023. By adopting ERC-223, our platform ensures users have full control over their tokens during the exchange process, eliminating the need for traditional approval steps. This not only enhances security but can also reduce GAS costs by up to 15% in certain transactions.
erc223Support.marginTrading: Additionally, ERC-223 paves the way for implementing our “Encapsulated Margin Trading” feature, further expanding the scope of decentralized finance on the platform.
erc223Support.erc20Fallback: For users who still prefer ERC-20, the exchange will maintain full support alongside ERC-223, allowing a seamless fallback whenever necessary. As EIP-7417 moves toward standardization, it will enable ERC-20 and ERC-223 tokens to be used interchangeably. Through a simple wrapping process, any existing ERC-20 token can be upgraded to an ERC-223 equivalent, bolstering fund security. These wrapped tokens and their original ERC-20 counterparts will share unified liquidity pools, delivering both convenience and confidence to all participants.
erc223Support.lede: ERC-223 fixes a core ERC-20 flaw and removes the approval step.

autoListings.heading: Transparent Auto-Listings
autoListings.description: DEX223 empowers users to freely import any existing token list from <tokenlists>tokenlists.org</tokenlists> or integrate new tokens directly through <autolisting>our auto-listing contract</autolisting>. This open, permissionless approach allows anyone to list a token without seeking approval from the exchange team or intermediaries. Acting as a decentralized alternative to traditional token lists, the auto-listing contract collects listing fees that are then distributed among DEX223 token holders as revenue. Through on-chain voting, the community also determines listing fees, reinforcing collective governance and ensuring that DEX223 remains transparent, inclusive, and owned by its users.
autoListings.lede: Anyone can list a token. No permission from the exchange team needed.

Allocation.heading: Tokenomics

paragraphs.inspiration: DEX223’s tokenomics draws inspiration from <link>Ethereum’s highly successful launch</link> model, emphasizing both security and sustainability. The original D223 tokens were issued in November 2023 on the Ethereum mainnet. From the moment DEX223 is launched, a fee will be charged on every on-platform trade, and those fees will be redistributed proportionally among D223 token holders.
paragraphs.unsoldTokens: Any tokens that remain unsold will be removed from the total supply. For instance, if 32% of platform tokens are sold, the existing tokens will claim that revenue, effectively treating the remaining 68% as non-existent. Decision will be made by DEX223 DAO on redistribution of unsold tokens from pre-ICO or public rounds.
paragraphs.transparency: In the spirit of financial transparency, the development team commits to publishing <link>monthly report</link> detailing the distribution and use of any funds collected through ICO events or private sales, ensuring that every aspect of DEX223’s growth and progress remains visible to the community.

structure.heading: DEX223 consists of multiple components that work together to create a secure, truly decentralized trading environment:

smartContract.title: DEX223 smart-contract
smartContract.description: This smart contract drives all core logic of the exchange. Once deployed, it operates autonomously, ensuring trades, fees, and governance procedures run smoothly without reliance on a centralized team.

webInterface.title: DEX223 web interface
webInterface.description: An "official" user interface is developed by the exchange team, but anyone can build an alternative UI that interacts with the DEX223 smart contract. This openness encourages innovation and user choice, empowering the community to shape their own trading experiences.

autoListing.title: Auto-listing smart-contracts
autoListing.description: DEX223 maintains at least three "default" auto-listing contracts with different fee structures. These contracts make token listings permissionless: as soon as a user pays the specified fee, the token appears for trading. A user may enable or disable specific auto-listing contracts at any time, which affects which tokens are visible in the interface. However, once a token is listed via one of these contracts, it cannot be delisted from that contract.

arbitraryAutoListing.title: Arbitrary auto-listing contracts
arbitraryAutoListing.description: Anyone is free to deploy a custom auto-listing contract with unique rules and fee settings. The DEX223 UI recognizes these third-party contracts when a user provides the contract address. This model fosters complete decentralization and mitigates the need for gatekeepers.

liquidationBots.title: Auto-liquidation bots
liquidationBots.description: Lenders on DEX223 manually trigger liquidations, yet they can set a fee to reward anyone who calls the liquidation function. This incentive allows third-party bots to monitor positions across the exchange and execute liquidations reliably. The exchange team develops a reference script for this task, but the system remains open to custom solutions.

ecosystem.intro: While not part of the DEX223 exchange itself, several initiatives bolster the adoption of the ERC-223 standard:

lossesCalculator.description: A script that calculates “lost” ERC-20 tokens in real time, demonstrating how ERC-223 enhances safety and reduces errors common with the older standard.

erc20Security.heading: Security problems of ERC-20 standard
erc20Security.lead: ERC-20 standard violates common secure software design principles which resulted in a loss of {amount} worth of tokens.
erc20Security.totalLost: Total amount of lost ERC-20 tokens
erc20Security.history: ERC-20 was designed in 2015. At that time there was a bug in EthereumVM. In order to make tokens not affected by this bug ERC-20 was designed in a clunky way which does not allow for error handling. <desktopOnly>As the result of impossibility of handling user mistakes $201M worth of ERC-20 tokens were lost.</desktopOnly>
erc20Security.erc223Security: ERC-223 is designed with security in mind. ERC-223 would allow to prevent user mistakes and we believe than in the long term a standard that prevents user mistakes and losses of funds will thrive.
erc20Security.lede: ERC-20 has no error handling, so one user mistake can lose tokens for good.

legacy.title: Built around a 2015 bug
legacy.text: Designed around an old EVM bug, it cannot handle errors.

fix.title: ERC-223 prevents mistakes
fix.text: Built with security in mind to stop user errors.

approveTransferFrom.heading: Security problems of approve & transferFrom pattern
approveTransferFrom.lead: Transacting method of ERC-20 tokens can put users funds at risk by authorizing DEX contract to operate funds on users behalf.
approveTransferFrom.description: ERC-20 tokens require approval before depositing to smart contracts, as approval and swap are separate transactions. To save GAS and enhance user experience, DEXes suggest issuing unlimited approvals once. However, this gives the contract ongoing control over the tokens, risking loss if the contract is hacked, even years later.
approveTransferFrom.erc223Solution: ERC-223 tokens can be swapped without approvals. The user has the control over their ERC-223 tokens at any moment and no third party is authorized to make transfers on users behalf.
approveTransferFrom.warning: An approval must be issued every time you perform a swap. If an exchange prompts you to issue a one-time approval then it authorizes the contracts to do anything with your tokens forever.
approveTransferFrom.lede: ERC-20 approvals let a DEX contract move your tokens on your behalf.

unlimited.title: Unlimited approvals
unlimited.text: Approving once to save GAS gives the contract ongoing control.

hack.title: Risk lasts for years
hack.text: If that contract is ever hacked, your tokens can be lost.

noApproval.title: ERC-223 needs no approval

Fight.heading:
ERC-20 vs ERC-223:

A Clash of Token Standards
Fight.intro: Since 2017, a heated debate has raged over which standard, ERC-20 or ERC-223, offers a safer, more seamless experience. The core issue revolves around how tokens and Ether are deposited into externally owned addresses (controlled by individuals) versus smart contracts.

points.erc223: Ether and ERC-223 automatically detect whether the recipient is an externally owned address or a contract, choosing the right deposit method accordingly.
points.erc20: ERC-20, however, places the burden on the user to pick the correct transfer method. If the wrong path is chosen, the tokens are lost because the ERC-20 standard lacks a proper transaction handling model.

Fight.learnMore: To learn more about this ongoing rivalry and its impact on the broader ecosystem, visit the <link>ERC-223 front page</link> to uncover the full history since 2017.
Fight.lede: Since 2017, one question: which standard keeps tokens safe?

erc223.title: ERC-223 knows the recipient
erc223.text: It picks the right deposit method automatically.

erc20.title: ERC-20 leaves it to you
erc20.text: Pick the wrong method and the tokens are lost.

Innovation.heading: Innovating decentralized trading
Innovation.description: DEX223 introduces a number of revolutionary concepts that no other exchange implements in the same way currently. These features will drastically improve the security, make token listings as easy and transparent as possible and allow on-platform lending of assets.

security.heading: Uncompromising security
security.text: The safety of user funds is paramount. Every component, from smart contracts to the interface, must be designed and audited to eliminate single points of failure. Our encapsulated margin trading system and auto-listing mechanisms are built with a proactive approach to security, reducing exposure to malicious activities and user errors alike.

economicSustainability.heading: Economic sustainability
economicSustainability.text: The platform’s incentive models, such as the revenue-sharing program from listing fees and lending order interest, are aimed at sustainable growth. By sharing rewards with DEX223 token holders, we cultivate a symbiotic relationship between protocol success and investor engagement.

decentralization.heading: True decentralization
decentralization.text: We envision an application that can operate indefinitely, free from external intervention or centralized oversight. Through smart-contract-driven listings, protocol-level governance, and distributed development, DEX223 aims to ensure that each step of trading, lending, and token listing is trustless and transparent.
decentralization.summary: Smart contracts, not a company, run every step.

educating.heading: Educating and empowering users
educating.text: DEX223 is committed to fostering a secure environment through clear documentation, step-by-step tutorials, and accessible user interfaces. Educating users about safe trading practices and platform risks empowers them to navigate the DeFi space with confidence.

permissionless.heading: Permissionless innovation
permissionless.text: DEX223 embraces a model where anyone can build upon or integrate with our protocol. Tokens can be freely listed, and new financial instruments, like encapsulated margin trading, are made available to all participants without gatekeepers. This openness fosters ongoing experimentation and creativity in the ecosystem.

governance.text: Holders of DEX223’s token are at the forefront of decision-making. This community-first design encourages transparent evolution of our protocol.

longTermVision.heading: Long-term vision
